error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the render service. Install and start the Scene Renderer add-on first, then try again — or check the service URL.

data_description.cameras: Cameras to render. All are selected by default; an empty selection means all.

cameras.description: The scene has {count} cameras: {camera_list}. Each selected camera gets its own image entity. Pick the ones you want to see.
cameras.title: Choose cameras

lights.description: The model has {count} named lights. Pick a Home Assistant light for each one you want to follow live. A light left empty renders at its model default (full brightness, model color).
lights.title: Map lights

data_description.name: Name for this scene (used for the device and entities).
data_description.service_url: Base URL of the render service, e.g. http://a1b2c3d4-scene-renderer:3000. Leave the discovered value unless you run the service somewhere else.
data_description.sun_enabled: Light the scene with the real sun position from the sun entity, in addition to your lights.

user.description: Connect to the Scene Renderer add-on. The add-on must be installed and started first — it does the rendering. The service URL is usually filled in automatically from the Supervisor.
user.title: HA Scene Renderer

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the render service. Is the Scene Renderer add-on running?

data_description.cameras: Cameras to render, one image entity each. An empty selection means all.
data_description.service_url: Base URL of the render service.
data_description.sun_enabled: Light the scene with the real sun position from the sun entity.

init.description: The light and camera lists are re-read from the add-on, so a changed model shows up here. Pick a Home Assistant light per model light; empty means the model default. Changing the camera selection adds or removes image entities.
init.title: Scene Renderer options
